parole.testo: Borrowed during the Hussite Wars (early 15th c.) from Old Czech haufnicě (modern Czech houfnice). Compare modern German Haufen, modern Czech houf (“flock, crowd”). Early German forms were huffnitze, hauffenicz. The current form with -b- appears around 1700.

parole.significato: socage (compulsory labor for serfs in feudalism)
parole.testo: From Middle High German robāt, robāte (also robbath, robolten (dative)), from Old Czech (compare Czech robota).

Inherited from Middle High German stigliz, stigelitze, from Old Czech stehlec, derived from Proto-Slavic *ščegъlъ. Cognate with modern Czech stehlík, Slovak stehlík, Polish szczygieł, Ukrainian щи́голь (ščýholʹ), Russian щего́л (ščegól), all referring to the same bird.
